draft.title: Visual techniques
card: Salience
the part of an image the eye goes to first. Size, bright colour, sharp focus and a central position can all make something salient.
Colour
colour can set a mood or draw attention. Warm colours such as red and orange often feel energetic or urgent. Cool colours such as blue often feel calm or distant.
Framing
how close the subject is and how much of the scene is shown. A close-up brings the viewer near a face. A wide shot shows the setting around a person.
Vectors and gaze

vectors are lines, such as an arm, a road or a pointing finger, that lead the eye along a path. Gaze is where a person in the image looks. It can lead the eye to an object, or look straight out at the viewer.
draft.remember: Visual techniques guide where a viewer looks first, what they feel and where their eye travels next.

a.q: A poster for a school swimming carnival has a huge, bright yellow swimmer at its centre and small grey text at the edges. What is the swimmer an example of?
opts: Salience, because the eye goes there first
Framing, because the text is at the edges
A vector, because the swimmer is in the centre
Gaze, because the swimmer is bright yellow
a.why: The swimmer is large, bright and central, so the eye goes there first. That is salience. Framing is about how close or wide the shot is, not about which part is noticed first.
a.clue: Ask which part the eye reaches first.

b.q: A poster for a charity shows a girl in the middle of the image looking at a bowl of food on the right. Viewers' eyes move from her face to the bowl. Which technique leads their eyes to the bowl?
opts: Her gaze, which points towards the bowl
Colour, because the girl's face is warm
Framing, because the bowl is on the right
Salience, because the bowl is the first thing seen
b.why: The girl looks at the bowl, so her gaze leads the viewer's eye there. The eye went to her face first, so she is the salient part, not the bowl. Framing is about how close the shot is, not about which way a person looks.
b.clue: Think about where the girl is looking.

a.best: Salience, because the eye goes there first

b.best: Her gaze, which points towards the bowl

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is the only one not written as 'Technique, because…', and it echoes the stem's 'looking at'. The clue 'Think about where the girl is looking' then points straight to it, so a student could pick it without knowing what gaze is.
